title: soft-termination-tombstone-and-resume-negotiator-openai-compat
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds soft-termination tombstone markers and a resume-negotiation handshake to make client disconnects and reconnects more resilient for streaming API calls; OpenAI compatibility adapter updated to expose continuation tokens and structured-output markers.
description:
Context and motivation: Streaming client disconnects during multi-step tool/function calls result in partial side-effects and poor developer experience: clients either lose progress or trigger duplicate tool calls on reconnect. This PR introduces a soft-termination 'tombstone' mechanism plus a handshake-based resume negotiator so clients can rejoin or safely abort without inducing duplicate effects. This is implemented as a compatibility-layer extension (opt-in via the OpenAI adapter header) and defaults to conservative behavior to avoid breaking existing contracts.

What this changes (single continuous description): Implements a server-side tombstone marker for streams that have been soft-terminated by the server after a grace window. A tombstone is a short-lived, idempotency-friendly marker recorded for an in-flight session that (1) records the last-acknowledged stream offset, (2) encodes any pending tool-call signatures (non-sensitive hashes used for idempotency), and (3) exposes a resume_token to the client. On reconnect, the client sends resume_token + last_received_offset in the OpenAI-compat resume handshake. The server negotiator validates the token against the tombstone; if valid, the server resumes by streaming from the negotiated offset and replays any structured-output markers necessary to reconstruct the partial call context. If tombstone TTL has expired or validation fails, the server falls back to either: (A) returning a hard-abort error that includes a safe re-run suggestion, or (B) offering a server-side replay path (controlled by customer policy).

Design highlights: - Soft-termination grace_window: configurable per-customer; default 30s. During grace window the server keeps a small in-memory KV entry with tombstone metadata and writes a condensed tombstone entry to the durable session store on soft-termination. - Tombstone contents: last_offset (int), stream_version (v2), tool_call_signature_hash (sha256 of tool id + args fingerprint), structured-output boundary markers (byte offsets), and expiry timestamp (ISO8601). Tombstones intentionally do NOT store plaintext inputs/outputs to avoid PII/Audit surface. - Resume negotiator: new state machine in api/openai/compat_streaming.go that accepts resume tokens and performs deterministic validation. Validation includes timestamp TTL check, stream_version compatibility, and tool_call_signature collision checks. - Idempotency: tool runtimes check tombstone signature hash to ensure re-run safety. If a tool is non-idempotent and tombstone suggests it may have executed, negotiator responds with 'resume_not_safe' and client can choose to force a re-run with acknowledgement header. - Structured output: streaming markers were extended to include a continuation boundary tag (CONT-BND:v2) so SDKs can reconstitute partial JSON/structured blobs across resume. This keeps the OpenAI-style streaming framing, but adds metadata that Redwood SDKs interpret for safe restarts.

Implementation notes: - Files added/changed (high level): src/streaming/terminate_manager.go (new tombstone writer + TTL sweeper), api/openai/compat_streaming.go (resume handshake and token validation), runtime/tool/idempotency.go (signature helpers), docs/api/streaming.md (spec), tests/integration/stream_resume_test.go (end-to-end). - Resume token format: base64url(JSON{session_id, tombstone_id, mac}). Tokens are MACed using per-tenant signing key; signing is pluggable through KMS. - Backwards compatibility: clients that do not pass the new header receive existing behavior; the tombstone/resume flow only activates when either: (a) client sends header X-Redwood-Resume: 1 on initial handshake, or (b) customer opts-in via tenant flag. - Security and privacy: tombstones avoid storing payloads; signing and TTL prevent replay attacks. We added KMS-backed signing for production tenants. - Observability: new metrics (stream.tombstone.created, stream.resume.attempts, stream.resume.succeeds, stream.resume.failures, stream.tombstone.ttl_expired) and tracing spans for the negotiation path.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for terminate_manager + negotiator, integration test covering resume success/failure, fuzz test for malformed tokens. Canary rollout plan: feature flagged by tenant; start with internal Redwood tenants, then 5 customers in canary cohort, ramp to 50% of traffic with monitoring thresholds on resume failure rates and tool duplicate signals.

Checklist: - [x] Tombstone writer and TTL sweeper implemented - [x] Resume handshake implemented in OpenAI adapter - [x] Tool signature and idempotency checks added - [x] Structured-output continuation markers finalized - [x] Tests added (unit + integration) - [x] Docs updated with example handshake and SDK guidance - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Compatibility and SDK work: Redwood SDKs will add helpers to: (1) detect CONT-BND:v2 markers and buffer structured payloads, (2) automatically send resume_token on reconnect when available, and (3) expose resume prompts in higher-level chat/session objects. This PR includes the API-side compatibility bits and docs examples; SDK PRs will follow.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: Tombstone retention increases memory/storage pressure. Mitigation: tombstones are condensed metadata only; sweeper and TTL aggressive by default (30s) and configurable. - Risk: Incorrect tool signature collisions could prevent safe resume. Mitigation: signature includes arg fingerprinting + tool runtime id; we also log collision diagnostics and expose developer-facing reason codes. - Risk: Behavior drift for older clients. Mitigation: opt-in via header and tenant flag; default unchanged.

Related work items: Linear ENG-1982 (streaming resume design), ENG-2045 (tool idempotency upgrades), SUP-482 (customer incident that motivated tombstone approach).

Commit summary: - add terminate_manager and tombstone format - implement resume_negotiator in compat adapter - add idempotency helpers to tool runtime - wire metrics and tracing - docs and integration tests

Changed files (high level list): src/streaming/terminate_manager.go, api/openai/compat_streaming.go, runtime/tool/idempotency.go, docs/api/streaming.md, tests/integration/stream_resume_test.go, go.mod

CI and rollout history: Initial CI run failed on a race in terminate_manager sweeper (flaky test). Fixed by adding a deterministic clock in tests and reworked sweeper locking. CI green after rerun; e2e integration in staging passed. Canary started 2025-01-20 with internal tenants; no duplicate tool signals observed in first 48h.

Merge notes: squashed commits to keep history concise. Feature lives behind tenant flag + opt-in header; not enabled by default for all customers. SDK teams notified to prepare adapters.
